summary.headline: The coconut boom fades: owners back in the red for the quarter
summary.text: Renuka Foods (COCO.N0000 voting, COCO.X0000 non-voting) owns Richlife dairy and Shaw Wallace (canned fish, soya, snacks) outright and 53% of Renuka Agri Foods, the coconut-milk exporter. The July–September 2026 quarter was weak: revenue fell 24% to Rs 3.78bn as coconut exports dropped, gross margin fell to 16.9% (24.2% a year earlier), and owners made a loss of Rs 26m (EPS −Rs 0.07) against a Rs 493m profit. Consumer brands slipped to a loss of roughly Rs 93m in the quarter, while most of the agri-foods profit now goes to Renuka Agri Foods' minority shareholders. For the six months, owners' profit was Rs 79m (Rs 576m), so the last twelve months' owners' profit is only about Rs 72m (Rs 0.19 a share). Cash flow improved (Rs 465m from operations in six months), but the group put another Rs 420m into unlisted equity investments without saying what, and the family's Renuka Enterprises now holds 56.6% of the voting shares. At Rs 22.50 (CSE, 13 November 2026) the share trades at 1.25x its NAV of Rs 17.94 and about 118x trailing earnings. I've cut the normal-earnings, consumer-brands and ROE assumptions, and four methods now put fair value at about Rs 12.60 (from Rs 13.90), so the price is about 79% above it (the non-voting share at Rs 20.20 is about 60% above). I'd buy at up to Rs 10.70 and treat under Rs 9.40 as a strong buy. The business still passes only 1 of 4 tests: avoid for now.

highlights.title: July–September 2026 quarter (unaudited)
highlights.text: Revenue down 24% to Rs 3.78bn (Rs 4.97bn); gross margin 16.9% (24.2%). Finance costs up to Rs 199m (Rs 132m). Group profit Rs 65m (Rs 625m), but owners made a loss of Rs 26m (a Rs 493m profit a year earlier); EPS −Rs 0.07. Minority shareholders took Rs 91m.

highlights.title: Six months to September 2026
highlights.text: Revenue Rs 7.54bn (−14%), exports Rs 3.34bn (Rs 4.54bn). Group profit Rs 282m (Rs 705m); owners' profit Rs 79m (Rs 576m), EPS Rs 0.21. Agri foods earned Rs 244m (Rs 210m) but consumer brands only Rs 38m (Rs 496m), implying a loss of about Rs 93m in July–September.

highlights.title: Cash flow better, but more money into unlisted shares
highlights.text: Operating cash flow Rs 465m (−Rs 350m a year earlier), helped by lower receivables. Capex Rs 319m. The group spent Rs 420m on 'investment in equity instruments', taking them to Rs 1,202m; at March the only such holding was the Rs 782m stake in Renuka Enterprises, the family's management company. The report doesn't say what was bought. Net debt rose to Rs 2.61bn.

highlights.title: Stake changes
highlights.text: Renuka Foods put Rs 400m into an existing subsidiary, and Rs 152m moved from minority interests to owners' equity, suggesting a higher stake in a partly owned subsidiary (probably Renuka Agri Foods); not explained. Of the Rs 232m rise in owners' equity since March, Rs 152m came from this, not from profit.

highlights.title: Family consolidates control
highlights.text: Renuka Enterprises now holds 56.57% of the voting shares (46.06% in June). The 18m shares held jointly by Dr S.R. and Mrs I.R. Rajiyah are gone, and the 37.8m-share increase equals that holding plus the 5.51% previously shown for Renuka Holdings.

highlights.title: Accounts now start from the audited March figures
highlights.text: The September interim uses the audited March 2026 balance sheet (owners' equity Rs 6,511m; the June interim had started from an unaudited Rs 6,594m). April–June figures weren't changed. The year-earlier EPS comparatives (Rs 3.34 and Rs 3.77) are before the split and don't reconcile with the profits; EPS here is worked out from profit.

series.label: EPS (after the 2026 split)

methodReadings.reading: 1.25x NAV. A business earning 7–10% on equity in good years, and about 1% in the last twelve months, is worth less than its book value at a 17.5% required return. Rs 152m of the NAV rise since March came from a stake change, not profit.
9.5% in 2025/26 was the best year in four; the last twelve months fell to about 1% as coconut margins eased and consumer brands lost money.
Trailing owners' profit is only about Rs 72m. Even on a recovered normal EPS of Rs 1.10, the price is 20x earnings against a 12.4% government bond.
Rs 0.19 for 2025/26, about half in new shares; nothing for the two years before. Too small to value on.

Renuka Agri Foods stake Rs 12.40 a share at market, consumer brands Rs 5–11 after their loss in the September quarter, plus other assets less debt. The most generous method, but Renuka Agri Foods itself is priced on a boom year.
Book value Rs 17.94 earning 5–11% against a 16.5–18.5% required return: lowest method.

modelsNote: Earnings swing with coconut prices and cash flow has been weak, so no DCF. The sum of the parts (anchored on Renuka Agri Foods' market price) is the most generous method; residual income, which charges for the low returns, is the least. Normal EPS, consumer-brands value and ROE were cut after the September quarter.

scenarios.common: 10-year government bond about 12.4% (9 Nov 2026). Base cost of equity = bond + about 5 points for a family-controlled food group with cyclical earnings. Normal EPS assumes some recovery from the last twelve months (Rs 0.19) but not back to the 2025/26 peak (Rs 1.62).

buyPlan.note: About Rs 5,535 in total, against Rs 11,250 at Rs 22.50 (Rs 10,100 for the non-voting share at Rs 20.20). Prices apply to either share class.
buyPlan.realism: Rs 10.70 needs about a 52% fall (47% for the non-voting share). This year the voting share has traded at Rs 22.00–34.00 and the non-voting at Rs 19.10–28.50, so the buy price is well outside the range. A return there would probably need the coconut earnings to fall further and the market to give up on a recovery.

notes.disclaimer: These are estimates from the 2024/25 and 2025/26 annual reports and the interim reports to September 2026 (unaudited). This is analysis, not personal financial advice.

Decision box.Verdict: Overpriced: about 79% above fair value of Rs 12.60 (non-voting about 60% above).
Decision box.Expected yearly return at Rs 22.50: About −12% a year over three years: dividend 0.8% + book growth about 5% − about 18% a year if the price moved to fair value.
Decision box.Downside / upside: Bear case −62% (Rs 8.60); bull case −21% (Rs 17.90). Even the bull case is below today's price.
Decision box.What the price assumes: Owners' ROE of about 20% for ten years, or Rs 1.90 of EPS every year at 12x: ten times the last twelve months.
Decision box.Confidence: Low to medium: the methods give Rs 8–18 in the base case; earnings depend on coconut prices, and the group's stake deals are poorly explained.
Decision box.Margin of safety: Buy 15% below fair value (Rs 10.70), strong buy 25% below (Rs 9.40).

Business and moat.What it does: Agri foods (57% of 2025/26 revenue): Renuka Agri Foods and Renuka Agri Organics make coconut milk, cream and other coconut products, mostly for export to Europe and the Middle East. Consumer brands (43%): Richlife dairy (milk, yoghurt, cheese), Shaw Wallace (Renuka Captain and Plaza canned fish, soya, cereals, snacks, juices).
Business and moat.Segment profit 2025/26: Agri foods Rs 209m (a Rs 218m loss in 2024/25); consumer brands Rs 460m (a Rs 159m loss); both after tax and before minority interests.
Business and moat.Moat: Narrow: private-label and B2B export relationships, Richlife's brand (7th dairy brand by Kantar, 35,000 outlets), Shaw Wallace's distribution. Coconut supply and prices are outside its control.
Business and moat.Ownership of subsidiaries: Richlife 100%, Shaw Wallace 98.9%, Renuka Agri Foods 53.0% (76.0% a year earlier).
Business and moat.Segment profit April–September 2026: Agri foods Rs 244m (Rs 210m a year earlier); consumer brands Rs 38m (Rs 496m), about −Rs 93m in July–September. Both after tax and before minority interests. Segment revenue: agri Rs 3.51bn (Rs 4.77bn), consumer brands Rs 4.04bn (Rs 4.00bn).

Management and governance.Ownership: Renuka Enterprises (Pvt) Ltd 56.57% of voting shares at 30 September 2026 (46.06% in June); CJ Patel 8.37%, Eagle View 7.56%, Cargo Boat Investment 3.06%. The Rajiyah family's joint 18m shares (5.00%) and, it appears, Renuka Holdings' 5.51% moved to Renuka Enterprises. Ultimate parent: Renuka Holdings PLC. Public float 31.99% of voting shares.
Management and governance.Related parties: Rs 782m paid in 2025/26 for 16% of Renuka Enterprises, the group's management company and Renuka Foods' largest shareholder; a further Rs 420m of equity investments in April–September 2026, not explained. Royalty of Rs 89m to Renuka International Ltd and Rs 14.4m rent, both director-linked. Key management pay Rs 265m in 2025/26 (Rs 169m).
Management and governance.Reporting quality: Interims now start from audited balances, but the year-earlier EPS comparatives are pre-split and don't reconcile with the profits, and the stake changes and new equity investments in the September quarter aren't explained.

Sri Lanka checks.Coconut prices: Risk: the main driver of agri profits; exports fell 27% in April–September 2026; shortages caused the 2023/24 and 2024/25 losses.
Sri Lanka checks.Exports and trade: Watch: 44% of revenue is exported; US tariffs and EU deforestation rules are risks; a weaker rupee helps.
Sri Lanka checks.Interest rates: Watch: Rs 3.2bn of short-term loans; finance costs Rs 199m in July–September (Rs 132m).
Sri Lanka checks.Consumers: Watch: consumer brands slipped to a loss in July–September despite flat sales; household spending is value-focused.
Sri Lanka checks.Liquidity: OK for the voting share; thin for the non-voting share.
Sri Lanka checks.Catalysts: December 2026 quarter (due by mid-February), coconut crop and prices, what the Rs 1.2bn of equity investments are, any further related-party deals.

Portfolio fit.Cost of 500 shares: About Rs 11,250 now; about Rs 5,350 at the buy price.
Portfolio fit.Overlap: Renuka Holdings (on the site) is Renuka Foods' ultimate parent; holding both doubles the exposure.
Portfolio fit.Note: Shown for information, not as advice on how much to hold.

Investment case and sell rules.Why own it: Only at a deep discount: a coconut exporter and dairy brand with moderate debt, if earnings recover.
Investment case and sell rules.The case is broken if: More value goes to related family companies, or coconut margins collapse again.
Investment case and sell rules.Sell triggers: Price more than 30% above fair value (above Rs 16.40: today's price is above this).

Key ratios (five-year trend).Net debt: Mar 2025 Rs 4.4bn · Mar 2026 Rs 2.4bn · Jun 2026 Rs 2.4bn · Sep 2026 Rs 2.6bn
Key ratios (five-year trend).Interest cover: 2021/22 4.4x · 2022/23 0.9x · 2023/24 −0.2x · 2024/25 0.2x · 2025/26 2.9x (company figures) · Apr–Sep 2026 about 1.1x (operating profit ÷ finance costs)

What this analysis doesn't cover: Renuka Agri Foods' own reports (only the consolidated figures were read); its latest share price (Rs 10.90 from 11 November 2026 is used) and whether Renuka Foods' 53% stake changed in the September quarter.
What the Rs 420m of new equity investments and the Rs 400m put into a subsidiary were.
Why finance income was Rs 294m in April–September 2026 while only Rs 37m of interest was received in cash.
The terms behind the Renuka Trading share deal in note 18.4 of the 2025/26 annual report, which are hard to follow.
fullText:
Summary: Renuka Foods (COCO.N0000 voting, COCO.X0000 non-voting) owns Richlife dairy and Shaw Wallace (canned fish, soya, snacks) outright and 53% of Renuka Agri Foods, the coconut-milk exporter. The July–September 2026 quarter was weak: revenue fell 24% to Rs 3.78bn as coconut exports dropped, gross margin fell to 16.9% (24.2% a year earlier), and owners made a loss of Rs 26m (EPS −Rs 0.07) against a Rs 493m profit. Consumer brands slipped to a loss of roughly Rs 93m in the quarter, while most of the agri-foods profit now goes to Renuka Agri Foods' minority shareholders. For the six months, owners' profit was Rs 79m (Rs 576m), so the last twelve months' owners' profit is only about Rs 72m (Rs 0.19 a share). Cash flow improved (Rs 465m from operations in six months), but the group put another Rs 420m into unlisted equity investments without saying what, and the family's Renuka Enterprises now holds 56.6% of the voting shares. At Rs 22.50 (CSE, 13 November 2026) the share trades at 1.25x its NAV of Rs 17.94 and about 118x trailing earnings. I've cut the normal-earnings, consumer-brands and ROE assumptions, and four methods now put fair value at about Rs 12.60 (from Rs 13.90), so the price is about 79% above it (the non-voting share at Rs 20.20 is about 60% above). I'd buy at up to Rs 10.70 and treat under Rs 9.40 as a strong buy. The business still passes only 1 of 4 tests: avoid for now.

Price and key figures
Price: Rs 22.50 voting, Rs 20.20 non-voting (CSE, 13 November 2026). July–September range Rs 22.00–28.70 (non-voting Rs 19.10–26.00); April–June Rs 24.90–34.00.
2025/26 (audited): revenue Rs 18.0bn, group profit Rs 669m, owners' profit Rs 568m, EPS Rs 1.62, owners' ROE 9.5%, NAV Rs 17.38.
July–September 2026 (unaudited): revenue Rs 3.78bn (−24%), gross margin 16.9% (24.2%), group profit Rs 65m (Rs 625m), owners' loss Rs 26m (profit Rs 493m), EPS −Rs 0.07.
April–September 2026: revenue Rs 7.54bn (−14%), owners' profit Rs 79m (Rs 576m), EPS Rs 0.21, operating cash flow Rs 465m. NAV Rs 17.94. Net debt Rs 2.61bn (0.28x equity). Twelve-month owners' profit about Rs 72m (EPS about Rs 0.19).

Decision box
Fair value about Rs 12.60 (was Rs 13.90); price about 79% above it. Expected return at today's price about −12% a year over three years. Bear case −62%, bull case −21%. The price assumes owners' ROE of about 20%. Buy up to Rs 10.70, strong buy under Rs 9.40.

Valuation table (Rs per share)
Method | Bear | Base | Bull | Weighted
P/E | 4.8 | 11.0 | 19.2 | 10.8
Price to NAV | 10.8 | 14.3 | 17.9 | 14.0
Sum of the parts | 13.1 | 18.0 | 22.9 | 17.5
Residual income | 5.6 | 8.1 | 11.4 | 8.0
Average | 8.6 | 12.9 | 17.9 | 12.6

Assumptions
Cost of equity 18.5% / 17.5% / 16.5%. Normal EPS Rs 0.60 / 1.10 / 1.60 at 8 / 10 / 12 times (was 0.90 / 1.40 / 1.90). 0.6x / 0.8x / 1.0x NAV. Renuka Agri Foods stake at market (Rs 10.90) less 40% / 25% / 10%; consumer brands Rs 5 / 8 / 11 a share (was 7 / 10 / 12). Owners' ROE 5% / 8% / 11% (was 6 / 9 / 12).

What changed
The September quarter showed the coconut boom fading (exports down 27% for the half year, gross margin 16.9%) and consumer brands slipping to a loss, leaving owners with about Rs 72m of profit over twelve months. I cut normal EPS, the consumer-brands value and the ROE range; NAV rose to Rs 17.94, partly from a Rs 152m transfer from minority interests.

Concerns
Two losses in five years and an owners' loss in the latest quarter, negative cash flow over three years, tiny dividends, Rs 1.2bn now in unlisted equity investments (Rs 782m of it in the family's management company, which is Renuka Foods' largest shareholder, and Rs 420m added this half without explanation), key management pay of Rs 265m, and audit adjustments that cut 2025/26 group profit by 39% from the March interim.

Business tests: 1 of 4 passed (debt; fails returns, steady profit and cash conversion), so it's a weak business: avoid for now (unchanged).

500-share plan
200 shares up to Rs 12.60, 150 up to Rs 10.70, 150 up to Rs 9.40: average about Rs 11.07, about Rs 5,535 in total. Rs 10.70 needs about a 52% fall (47% for the non-voting share).

Note: Renuka Holdings (also on the site) is Renuka Foods' ultimate parent, so holding both doubles the exposure.
